decisions.summary: Two rules of classify kept for a caption's own subject: a name in dark ink takes no dark fill it names; an area caption does not lie across its subject's drawn outline.
decisions.why: Unchanged from round 4 (each exception ruled separately against request.md and the entry: both are classify's own rules for the named subject, implied by the entry's 'builds its obstacle index with hand_sheet.classify'; OUTLINE measured to carry the 3 -> 7, so dropping it defeats the one-view purpose; DARK inert here, held hard on the hand sheets). Round 4's credit note applied: D4 now says the outline rule alone accounts for the 7 and the dark rule moves no seat. The new filter keeps both: outline bands are _band polygons, never the shape's own poly, and WEIGHT_DARK is excluded from the drop.

decisions.summary: Every obstacle classify gives for a declared shape is dropped from that caption's index, flagged inner or not (WEIGHT_DARK kept; outline bands are not the shape's polygon and stay); everything else blocks.
decisions.why: Round 4's item resolved. compound._one_view's kept line no longer tests o.inner, so the other mats a mats caption names and the other striking post are no longer obstacles to it - US2's 'never against its own parts' as D4 states it. Declared shapes are rects and circles (data-id on rect/circle), never line shapes whose obstacles are bands, so matching by tuple(o.poly) reaches every one. With the carve-out gone this is the requirement itself, not an exception: within. Harness re-run on the built code: unchanged (3 apart, as m:caption-disagreements-after records).
